title: Lowest-radiation environments in the Solar System: New opportunities for underground rare-event searches
abstract: We study neutrino, muon, and gamma-ray fluxes in extraterrestrial environments in our Solar System via semianalytical estimates and Monte Carlo simulations. In sites with negligible atmosphere, we find a strong reduction in the cosmic-ray-induced neutrino and muon fluxes relative to their intensities on Earth. Neutrinos with energies between 50 MeV and 100 TeV show particularly strong suppression, by as much as 10 3 , even at shallow depths. The solar neutrino suppression increases as the square of the site’s distance from the Sun. Natural radiation due to nuclear decay is also expected to be lower in many of these locations and may be reduced to effectively negligible levels in liquid water environments. The sites satisfying these characteristics represent an opportunity for greatly extending the physics reach of underground searches in fundamental physics, such as searches for weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter, neutrinoless double-beta decay, the diffuse supernova neutrinos, and neutrinos from nearby supernova. As a potential near-term target, we propose a measurement of muon and gamma-ray fluxes in an accessible underground lunar site such as the Mare Tranquillitatis pit to perform a first measurement of the prompt component in cosmic-ray-induced particle production, and to constrain lunar evolution models. Although the focus of this work is on fundamental physics, the finding of this work—that the existence of an atmosphere in a planet enhances cosmic-ray-induced radiation in its underground—could be relevant for a broader range of sciences, such as radiobiology deep underground and searches for extraterrestrial life.

title: Accurate Charge Radius Measurement of C 14 Confronts Ab Initio Theory
abstract: Located at the neutron shell closure N = 8 , the long-lived radioactive isotope C 14 plays a critical role in geochronology and nuclear structure studies. Despite its widespread use, the nuclear charge radius of C 14 has remained less precisely known than that of its stable counterpart C 12 . Here, we report a high-precision determination of the C 14 charge radius using collinear laser spectroscopy at the COALA setup at TU Darmstadt, improving upon the precision of previous muonic measurements by a factor of 5 and revealing a 1.9 σ discrepancy of combined uncertainty, indicating a likely underestimated uncertainty in the muonic determination. This measurement challenges state-of-the-art nuclear theory calculations, including auxiliary field diffusion Monte Carlo, the valence-space in-medium similarity renormalization group, and the no-core shell model, augmented by neural-network techniques. With C 12 and C 14 now forming one of the most precisely characterized even-even isotope pairs, these results also enable improved QED tests.

title: Measurement of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering on Germanium by COHERENT
abstract: The COHERENT Collaboration reports the most precise measurement of the coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering cross section to date. This measurement was performed with COHERENT’s germanium detector array, Ge-Mini, at the Spallation Neutron Source at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. A cumulative exposure of 4.69 × 10 22 protons on target yielded a total number of observed counts of 124 − 12 + 14 and a flux-averaged cross section of 0.98 ± 0.10 ( statistical ) ± 0.10 ( systematic ) relative to the standard-model expectation of 5.9 × 10 − 39 cm 2 . The well-understood energy and timing distributions of the neutrino source allow for independent measurements of muon- and electron-neutrino scattering rates. This information is used to improve constraints on nonstandard neutrino interactions mediated by heavy particles.

title: Updated 78mBr 2−→1+ lifetime from isomeric decay cascade in active target
abstract: The half-life of the 2 − state at 32.3 keV in 78 Br has been measured only twice, yielding mutually inconsistent values of (14.2 ± 3) ns and (8.3 ± 0.3) ns; the currently adopted value of (11.3 ± 0.3) ns is their unweighted average. We report a new measurement of this half-life using a self-coincidence technique in which both the 148.6 keV 4 + → 2 − and 32.3 keV 2 − → 1 + transitions of the 78m Br isomeric cascade are captured within single digitized waveforms from a LaBr3(Ce) active-target detector, following production via 79 Br(n,2n) 78m Br with a pulsed deuterium–tritium neutron source. We obtain half-lives of (118.45 ± 0.72) µs and (19.8 ± 0.4) ns for the 4 + → 2 − and 2 − → 1 + transitions, respectively. The method is validated by applying it to the analogous 5 − → 2 − → 1 + cascade in 80m Br, for which all measured half-lives agree with adopted values within 1σ. The new 2 − → 1 + half-life in 78m Br exceeds the adopted value by 15.96σ, implying a 43% reduction in the reduced electric-quadrupole transition probability B(E2; 2 − → 1 + ) relative to currently evaluated data. This substantially increased hindrance of the 2 − → 1 + transition constrains the structure of low-lying negative-parity states in 78 Br and motivates renewed shell-model and beyond-mean-field calculations in the neutron-deficient A ≃ 78 mass region, where shape coexistence and proton–neutron residual interactions are expected to play important roles.

title: Superheavy nuclei with Z = 119, 120: α-decay or spontaneous fission?
abstract: We propose a local formula for calculating α -decay energies Q α in superheavy nuclei (SHN) with atomic numbers Z > 110, achieving a mean deviation of only 0.026 MeV and thus providing high-precision Q α predictions for the heaviest nuclei. Using these calculated Q α values, α -decay half-lives are computed where the barrier is derived from the self-consistent Skyrme energy density functional, which are in excellent agreement with available experimental data. For spontaneous fission, we adopt three independent approaches: a new formula with a good accuracy, a fission barrier penetration framework based on the Skyrme functional, and the generalized liquid-drop model with shell correction. The predicted dominant decay modes for synthesized SHN with Z > 110 are consistent with experimental observations. As an encouraging result, α -decay is predicted to be the dominant decay mode for the candidate nuclei of as-yet-unsynthesized elements Z = 119 and 120, with half-lives of 0.2–0.6 ms for Z = 119 and 0.02–0.06 ms for Z = 120 , which are many orders of magnitude shorter than their corresponding spontaneous fission half-lives. This greatly facilitates the identification of elements 119 and 120. These results along with our methods offer valuable guidance for future experiments on the synthesis of new elements.

title: Improved calibration algorithm and its validation for Guide Tube Calibration System in JUNO experiment
abstract: The Guide Tube Calibration System (GTCS) of the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) is designed to calibrate the detector boundary non-uniformity, contributing to the stringent energy resolution requirement of JUNO. A 27Bq 241 Am- 9 Be neutron source is adopted for GTCS calibration, providing both point-like prompt signals from γ rays and spread-out delayed signals from neutron capture. This source is less affected by local optical shadowing and provides a prompt–delayed signature similar to inverse beta decay (IBD) and cosmogenic neutron events, enabling direct cross-checks. Additionally, realistic experimental conditions, including radioactive backgrounds and electronic noise are considered, so that a dedicated set of event selection criteria has been developed for GTCS. Comprehensive simulations and analyses under realistic background and noise conditions indicate that using 241 Am- 9 Be calibration source is feasible to meet the required 1% uncertainty for GTCS. Applying the improved GTCS calibration algorithm to experimental data collected on 23 August 2025, the energy responses at five calibration positions have been obtained, providing input to the detector non-uniformity correction function. The results have a good consistency with simulation, demonstrating the feasibility and robustness of the updated calibration approach.

title: Design of a high voltage delivery system for noble liquid time projection chambers
abstract: Noble liquid time projection chambers (TPCs) are a leading technology in the detection of ionizing radiation, particularly in applications such as accelerator neutrino physics, dark matter detection, and neutrinoless double beta decay. This paper addresses the design considerations for implementing stable high voltage (HV) systems within large noble liquid TPCs, with a focus on the nEXO experiment. Utilizing insights from prior HV research and experimental investigations, we outline factors influencing HV stability and discuss design choices to improve stability and prevent electrical discharges. A novel HV delivery system concept is presented, tailored for the nEXO TPC, which incorporates these design considerations while also meeting the stringent radiopurity requirements of the nEXO neutrinoless double beta decay search. These design considerations and their specific implementation towards a HV delivery system offer guidance to future experiments applying high voltage in noble liquid environments.

title: Cyclotron radiation signal characterization in resonant cavities for the Project 8 neutrino mass experiment
abstract: Many experimental methods in physics require understanding radiation from single particles into non-trivial electromagnetic mode structures. Such characterization is critical for Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy (CRES), an advancing new measurement technique that has the potential to greatly benefit fundamental physics measurements. In CRES, charged particles emit cyclotron radiation at frequencies that provide their energy measurement. As a notable example, the Project 8 experiment aims to kinematically infer the neutrino mass by measuring the energies of electrons emitted in tritium beta decay using CRES. In near-term realizations of Project 8, resonant cylindrical cavities will be used for CRES readout, in a configuration with a magnetic field oriented along the symmetry axis, and electrons following helical cyclotron trajectories confined to the cavity interior. The physics of electromagnetic radiation in these environments is complicated, since it involves both the motion of the emitting particle and the mode structure imposed by the cavity. In this work, we derive and validate an analytic model for how an oscillating, trapped electron radiates into cavity modes, and the power and frequency content of the radiation that can be read out from these events. These results can be used to guide the design of cavities for future CRES and other experiments.

title: Shell structure and spontaneous decay of superheavy Z = 124 isotopes with the deformed relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory in continuum
abstract: Shell structure and spontaneous decay of $Z = 124$ isotopes are systematically investigated using the deformed relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory in continuum (DRHBc) with the PC-PK1 density functional. By accounting for deformation and continuum effects, the neutron drip line is predicted to be located at $N = 320$, and eight potential multi-neutron emitters beyond the neutron drip line are identified. The results, compared with the spherically constrained case, highlight the critical role of deformation effects in determining the ground-state properties of superheavy nuclei. In addition, potential neutron shell closures emerge at $N = 258$ and $350$, alongside subshell closures at $N = 232$ and $320$. The results disfavor $Z = 124$ as a possible proton magic number and suggest $Z = 120$ and $138$ as more favorable candidates for proton shell closures in the superheavy region. Finally, the competition between $\alpha$ decay, $\beta$ decay, and spontaneous fission is analyzed by calculating half-lives within various semi-empirical formulas. The results indicate that $\alpha$ decay is the predominant mode on the proton-rich side, whereas spontaneous fission and $\beta^-$ decay gradually become dominant with increasing neutron number.

title: Dihadron Transverse-Spin Asymmetries in Muon-Deuteron Deep-Inelastic Scattering
abstract: In 2022, the COMPASS collaboration performed semi-inclusive measurements of deep-inelastic muon-scattering on a transversely polarized deuteron ( LiD 6 ) target. From these data, transverse-spin-dependent dihadron asymmetries are extracted using pairs of oppositely charged hadrons. These asymmetries are directly sensitive to the quark transversity distributions and provide an independent handle on these fundamental quantities with respect to the Collins asymmetries measured in single-hadron production. The present results significantly improve upon the previous COMPASS deuteron measurements, which were the only available deuteron data worldwide, and reach a statistical precision comparable to that of the existing proton results from COMPASS. A small but nonzero asymmetry is observed at large Bjorken- x , consistent with theoretical expectations. A point-by-point extraction of the valence-quark transversity distributions yields, in particular, a substantially improved determination of the d -quark transversity. These measurements represent a major step towards a complete flavor mapping of the transverse-spin structure of the nucleon.

title: Neutrinoless double-beta decay of the Δ − resonance
abstract: The subprocess n n → p p e − e − is a key ingredient in the interpretation of nuclear neutrinoless double- β decay. Intermediate Δ resonances may provide additional enhancements to this transition. We take a first step toward a Δ -full description of n n → p p e − e − by investigating the neutrinoless double- β decay Δ − → p e − e − in the framework of chiral effective field theory. We systematically derive the long-range contribution from light-Majorana-neutrino exchange through loop diagrams and incorporate the short-range part through counterterms required by renormalization. We predict the pion-mass dependence of the decay amplitude in the kinematic configuration with collinear electrons. Furthermore, to facilitate lattice-QCD matching, we calculate the decay amplitude in the degenerate Δ -nucleon mass limit and provide the corresponding long-range prediction.

title: Characterization and applications of the LaBr3 array at HUN-REN ATOMKI
abstract: A high-efficiency γ -ray spectrometer at HUN-REN Institute for Nuclear Research (HUN-REN ATOMKI), the LAnthanum Bromide Detector Array (LABDA) has been designed and constructed to study low-probability phenomena in particle physics, nuclear spectroscopy, and nuclear astrophysics experiments. The array is comprised of 12 cylindrically shaped LaBr 3 (Ce) crystals, each measuring 3 ′ ′ × 3 ′ ′ , produced by Saint-Gobain. Key performance parameters of the array have been systematically characterized over a broad γ -ray energy range (344–10762 keV), including energy resolution, energy non-linearity, detection efficiency, time resolution and intrinsic background. Intrinsic background suppression, using pulse-shape discrimination methods has been also investigated. The prospects for applying the array to different nuclear physics measurements are discussed.

title: A nanocomposite-mediated synergistic division inhibition strategy for selective antibacterial therapy against burn infections
abstract: Abstract Nanomaterial-based antibacterial therapy presents an alternative solution to antibiotic resistance. However, most research focuses on enhancing antibacterial activity while neglecting the selectivity of nanomaterials, leading to indiscriminate damage to mammalian cells. Here, we design a synergistic boron nitride-polydopamine@MOF-199 nanocomposite (BPM NC) that interferes with bacterial binary fission. Its selectivity stems from suppressing FtsZ polymerization during bacterial division, while its high efficiency arises from synergistic mechanisms such as disrupting membrane potential and bacterial defense systems. These effects induce molecular-level disruptions in bacterial biological processes, enabling BPM NC (0.35 μg/mL) to rapidly inactivate bacteria (10 7 CFU/mL) in 30 min—358-fold enhancement over its precursor h-BN. In burn infection models, BPM NC exhibits significant efficacy in male mice and female pigs, outperforming the clinical drug silver sulfadiazine. This work provides a promising insight into developing antibacterial nanomaterials that combine selectivity and high activity, offering a strategy for next-generation antibacterial therapies.

title: Direct measurement of the 59 Cu( p , α ) 56 Ni excitation function to constrain the NiCu cycle strength and its impact on explosive nucleosynthesis
First Simultaneous Analysis of Transverse Momentum Dependent and Collinear Parton Distributions in the Proton
abstract: We present the first simultaneous global QCD analysis of unpolarized transverse momentum dependent (TMD) and collinear parton distribution functions (PDFs) in the proton. Our Letter incorporates data from deep-inelastic scattering, Drell-Yan, inclusive weak boson, W + charm, and jet production involving PDFs, as well as TMD Drell-Yan and Z -boson production data from fixed target and collider experiments sensitive to both TMD and collinear distributions. The analysis is performed at next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy for QCD resummation in TMD observables and next-to-leading order for observables described in collinear factorization. The combined analysis improves knowledge of both TMD and collinear PDFs, particularly in the sea-quark sector, providing a consistent simultaneous description of the aforementioned observables.

title: First measurement of kaonic deuterium X-ray transitions
abstract: The study of the strong interaction among hadrons at low energies remains one of the key challenges in fundamental physics because of its non-perturbative nature, which makes theoretical descriptions strongly dependent on experimental input. Although substantial progress has been made for systems involving up and down quarks, theoretical models in the strangeness sector continue to face limitations due to the lack of experimental data. Kaonic atoms provide a powerful tool to study the low-energy strong interaction with strangeness through the energy shifts and widths induced on their lowest atomic levels. In this context, kaonic deuterium X-ray spectroscopy has long represented one of the major open challenges in hadronic-atom physics because of its extremely low X-ray yield. This measurement is particularly important because it gives access to the poorly constrained $K^-n$ interaction at threshold. Here, we report the first observation of kaonic deuterium X-ray transitions, performed with the SIDDHARTA-2 experiment at the DA$\Phi$NE collider. We determine the strong-interaction shift and width of the $1s$ level to be $\varepsilon_{1s}=-810.9\pm24.5\,(\mathrm{stat})\pm2.1\,(\mathrm{syst})\,\mathrm{eV}$ and $\Gamma_{1s}=812\pm97\,(\mathrm{stat})\pm33\,(\mathrm{syst})\,\mathrm{eV}$, respectively. This measurement constitutes the most precise experimental determination of the $K^-d$ strong interaction at threshold and allows discrimination among competing theoretical models. Combined with the kaonic hydrogen measurement, this result provides the experimental input required to determine the isospin-dependent $K^-N$ scattering lengths, with implications for the description of the nature of the molecular interpretation of the $\Lambda(1405)$, and neutron-rich matter.

title: Quantum theory of γ-transitions and nuclear deformation in radioactive 204−228Rn and 212−232Ra isotopes
abstract: The present study focuses on the radon and radium isotopic chains, specifically within the ranges 204 ≤ A ≤ 228 for radon and 212 ≤ A ≤ 232 for radium. These heavy nuclei undergo α, β, and γ decay. While the α-decay systematics are well established, the role of γ-transitions as probes of nuclear structure remains less understood. The main objective of this work is to explore the role of γ-transitions, the electric quadrupole moment Q0, and the deformation parameter β2 as effective probes into the internal structure of radon and radium nuclei, using a quantum electrodynamics framework combined with Fermi’s golden rule. Partial γ-decay widths, half-lives, mean lifetimes, and reduced transition probabilities B(E2) are derived from first principles and tabulated for all studied isotopes. The analysis reveals clear structural signatures across the chains, particularly near the neutron shell closure at N = 126 . A pronounced reduction in γ-decay half-lives is observed at and beyond this magic number, reflecting enhanced transition probabilities due to shell and collective effects. Our predictions for B(E2) values and deformation parameters are compared with existing experimental data and theoretical models (RMF, FRDM, global best-fit), showing overall good agreement while extending coverage to isotopes with limited experimental data. The evolution of Q0 and β2 indicates that nuclear deformation tends to be minimal when the neutron number approaches the magic value N = 126 , and increases progressively as the number of neutrons deviates from this closed-shell configuration. These results provide refined benchmarks for electromagnetic transition systematics in 204 − 228 Rn and 212 − 232 Ra, and demonstrate the predictive potential of quantum-transition models in regions critical for both nuclear structure and applied radiation science.

title: r -process nuclei in the rare-earth region above N = 126 in relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory: A preponderance of shape coexistence in nuclei
abstract: The shell structure of nuclei beyond N=126 relevant to the third peak at A ~ 195 in r-process nuclear abundances in investigated. Within the framework of the relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory in deformed space, a comparative study of the response of nuclei with three different model Lagrangians NL-SV1, SVI-2 and NL3 is made. Ground-state properties of even-even nuclei in the isotopic chains of Z=58-72$= in the highly neutron-rich region are investigated. A comparison of binding energies with mass formulas shows that in the extreme region of the r-process path, the RMF model SVI-2 without nonlinearities of sigma and omega mesons shows an excellent agreement with the mass formula HFB-24. It is shown that in all the above Lagrangian models, in the neutron rich region between the shell closures N=126 and N=184, there is a preponderance of nuclides exhibiting coexistence of well-deformed prolate and oblate shapes in the ground state. A prolate ground state is shown to evolve smoothly to a coexisting oblate ground state via a near degeneracy with successive addition of neutrons. Induced by an onset of deformation for $N \ge 130$, nuclei approaching the r-process path are shown to exhibit enhanced stability in many isotopic chains (Z > 60). This has the effect of shifting the expected neutron drip line significantly farther into the neutron-rich region especially for the higher Z chains. Consequences of the enhanced stability, the shape co-existence and degeneracy of shapes in nuclei on the r-process nucleosynthesis are discussed.

title: Anisotropic flow measurements in OO and Ne-Ne collisions with ALICE
abstract: The LHC results have demonstrated that small collision systems can exhibit collective behavior reminiscent of that~observed in heavy-ion collisions, opening a new frontier for exploring the connection between nuclear structure and collective dynamics at ultra-relativistic energies. However, the interpretation of collectivity in small collision systems is limited by understanding the proton subnucleonic structure. The ${}^{16}$O and ${}^{20}$Ne collisions delivered by the LHC offer an opportunity to study the influence of nuclear geometry on anisotropic flow in systems where the nuclear structure is well-constrained. In this proceeding, measurements of the anisotropic flow of charged particles, $v_n$, in OO and Ne-Ne collisions involving up to eight-particle correlations are presented, using the multi-particle cumulant method. Furthermore, the first reconstruction of the probability distribution function of elliptic flow $P(v_2)$, and the first measurement of the ratio $v_3\{4\}/v_3\{2\}$ in light-ion collision systems are reported. These measurements provide deeper insight into the role of nuclear geometry-driven flow in light-ion collisions.

title: New universal relations for magnetized neutron stars
abstract: Unlike the neutron-star mass--radius relation, which depends sensitively on the internal stellar structure through the equation of state of dense nuclear matter, certain neutron-star properties obey approximately universal relations that exhibit only weak dependence on the equation of state. In this paper, we explore new universal relations for magnetized neutron stars. We focus on a purely poloidal dipolar magnetic-field configuration and treat the effects of the magnetic field perturbatively to second order in the field strength. After appropriately normalizing the relevant quantities by the stellar mass and the magnetic-field strength at the pole, we first identify an exact universal relation between the magnetic dipole moment and stellar compactness. We then find approximate universal relations among the magnetic dipole moment, magnetically-induced stellar quadrupole moment, and ellipticity, with fractional variations due to the equation of state at the level of O(10%). We support these numerical findings with analytic estimates for Newtonian polytropes, which reproduce the observed behavior. Among the newly discovered relations, the one connecting the magnetic dipole moment and stellar quadrupole moment may be particularly useful for the analysis of gravitational-wave signals from binaries containing magnetized neutron stars.

title: Probing the neutron skin thickness through jet charge in deep-inelastic scattering
abstract: The neutron-skin thickness in neutron-rich nuclei has traditionally been measured using low-energy hadronic and electronic scatterings at hadronic level. In this paper, we propose an alternative probe to the neutron-skin thickness through deep-inelastic scattering in high-energy electron-ion collisions, leveraging the intrinsic correlation between final-state jet charge distribution and initial-state partonic distributions in nucleons. Specifically, we demonstrate the sensitivity of jet charge distribution to the neutron skin-thickness and density profile in e + Pb collisions with varying centralities as determined using Glauber model, and in isobar collisions of e + Ru and e + Zr . We predict a strong suppression of positive jet charge distribution and an enhancement for negative jet charge distribution in peripheral electron-ion collisions, revealing the neutron-skin effect. Premised on the effective determination of centrality, this proposal can also be extended to photon and -boson tagged jet charge distribution in proton-nucleus collisions at the Large Hadron Collider, providing another similar access to neutron-skin structure.

title: Optimization of β2 and β4 deformations for 176Yb using quasi-elastic barrier distribution
abstract: An effort has been made to optimize the quadrupole and hexadecapole deformation parameters for 176 Yb nuclei from the barrier distribution derived from quasi-elastic scattering measurements.The quasi-elastic excitation functions for the 14 N+ 176 Yb system were measured using the HYbrid Telescope ARray (HYTAR) detecting setup in the General Purpose Scattering Chamber (GPSC) at the Inter-University Accelerator Centre (IUAC), New Delhi. The barrier distribution for 14 N+ 176 Yb has been derived from the measured excitation functions. The experimental observables have been interpreted in light of full coupled channel calculations using the quantum mechanical code FRESCO. The coupled channel calculations for 14 N+ 176 Yb suggested that 176 Yb behaves as a rotational nucleus, and coupling up to the first three excited states with reported values of β2 and β4 explains the observed shape of the barrier distribution well. However, the deviation of coupled channel calculations from the precisely measured barrier distribution is further anticipated to have uncertain values for the considered deformation parameters, which have not been precisely reported in previous studies. The values of the deformation parameters β2 and β4 have been extracted using the chi-square minimization method. It has been found that β2=0.306 and β 4 = − 0.043 yielded the best fitted values to the experimental data. The present work strongly infers negative values for the hexadecapole deformation of 176 Yb and reports the values of β2=0.306 ± 0.002 and β 4 = − 0.043 ± 0.003 confidently up to three decimal places, which are consistent with those reported in the literature. Moreover, the optimized values have been corroborated by the angular distribution and fusion excitation function. The successful reproduction of the experimental observables, the angular distribution and fusion excitation function, through coupled channel calculations, substantiates the optimized values.

Unified description of the moments of inertia formulas in the Bohr and VMI models
abstract: A unified collective framework based on the Inglis formula for the nuclear moment of inertia is developed. In this approach, nuclear deformation is treated as a spin-dependent quantity that is determined self-consistently through total-energy minimization, with centrifugal stretching taken into account. In the small-deformation limit, an expansion about equilibrium yields a linear relationship between the moment of inertia and the deformation increment. This provides a microscopic foundation for Variable Moment of Inertia (VMI) models, without the need for explicit parameter mapping to quadrupole deformation. Coriolis effects are explicitly included. Bohr-type and VMI-type descriptions emerge as limiting cases of the same underlying framework.

title: Theoretical probe of deformed shell closure in α-Decay systematics of the superheavy region: 288,289Lv and 289Mc decay chains
abstract: A systematic study of α-decay half-lives along the decay chains of recently discovered 288 Lv and 289 Lv isotopes by Oganessian et al. [Phys. Rev. C 112 (2025) 014603], and 289 Mc is carried out using different effective nucleon–nucleon (B3Y, M3YR, M3YP, and the density-dependent DD-M3YP and CD-M3YP) interactions within both spherical and deformed configurations. The α–daughter interaction potential is calculated using the double-folding model, with the folding integral evaluated in momentum space via a Fourier transform. The penetration probability for ground-state to ground-state α- transitions is evaluated within the semiclassical WKB approximation, while the preformation probability is determined using the cluster formation model (CFM). The calculated logarithmic half-lives are compared with experimental data, and the role of nuclear deformation is examined through multipole deformation parameters of the daughter nuclei. The results show that deformation significantly modifies the interaction barrier by lowering its height and width, leading to enhanced penetrability and improved agreement with experimental half-lives. A pronounced structural effect is observed around N = 168 , which is attributed to the presence of a deformed shell closure in the superheavy region. Benchmark comparisons with the semi-empirical modified Brown and Royer formulae demonstrate that the microscopic double-folding calculations achieve superior agreement with the experimental α-decay half-lives and provide a more reliable description of the underlying structural properties along the investigated decay chains.

title: The STRASSE liquid hydrogen target system
abstract: A compact liquid hydrogen target system has been developed for the Silicon Tracker for RAdioactive nuclei Studies at SAMURAI Experiments (STRASSE) at the RIKEN Nishina Center. This target, designed for proton-induced quasi-free scattering measurements in inverse kinematics, features a customizable cylindrical cell with a volume up to 125 mL which increases the reaction rate/luminosity, and thin Mylar walls to minimize the protons’ angular straggling. The cryogenic system, operated at 20 K, is optimized for rapid cool-down ( ≤ 5 h) and empty-target measurements, avoiding long experimental dead time. This new setup will allow for high-precision studies of nuclear structure using both missing-mass and in-flight prompt γ -ray spectroscopy techniques at the RIBF facility.

title: Statistical effects of shape coexistence on fluctuation properties in even–even nuclei using the Berry–Robnik distribution
abstract: •A comprehensive statistical analysis of experimental low-lying levels (0⁺, 2⁺, 4⁺, 6⁺) across Z = 18–82 is performed using Berry–Robnik and Gaussian models.•Statistical indicators are interpreted as complementary measures of shape coexistence, not as independent signatures.•Mass-dependent evolution of Berry–Robnik q values reveals enhanced chaotic components in heavier nuclei.•Both reported and unreported E2-active states are included to ensure complete and unbiased level sequences.•Results demonstrate that configuration mixing associated with shape coexistence produces characteristic fluctuation patterns in nuclear spectra. Shape coexistence, arising from the presence of competing spherical, oblate, and prolate configurations at low excitation energies, is a key manifestation of structural complexity in atomic nuclei. Its spectroscopic fingerprints include anomalously low‑lying 0⁺ states, irregular band structures, and strong configuration mixing. In this work, we perform a systematic statistical analysis of experimentally measured low‑lying levels (0⁺, 2⁺, 4⁺, 6⁺) in even–even nuclei across Z = 18–82 to investigate the fluctuation properties associated with shape coexistence. After unfolding the spectra using a polynomial approximation to the cumulative level density, nearest‑neighbor spacing distributions were constructed and analyzed using Gaussian and Berry–Robnik models. The Gaussian variances extracted from the unfolded spacing distributions are σ² = 10.04 (2⁺₁), 4.78 (4⁺₁), 3.12 (6⁺₁), 4.38 (0⁺₂), 4.70 (2⁺₂), 2.27 (0⁺₃), and 3.81 (2⁺₃) across the full region Z = 18–82, with smaller values in lighter nuclei and larger fluctuations in heavier ones. Berry–Robnik fits yield q values close to the Wigner limit (q → 0): q = 0.056 (2⁺₁), 0.139 (4⁺₁), 0.086 (6⁺₁), 0.139 (0⁺₂), 0.152 (2⁺₂), 0.168 (0⁺₃), and 0.078 (2⁺₃) for Z = 18–82, indicating predominantly chaotic dynamics induced by shape coexistence. The mass‑dependent evolution of q, with heavier nuclei exhibiting stronger chaotic components, further supports the interpretation that shape coexistence generates mixed regular–chaotic dynamics. These results establish spectral‑fluctuation measures as a robust, model‑independent diagnostic of shape coexistence in atomic nuclei. It is emphasized that the statistical indicators extracted in this work are not introduced as independent signatures of shape coexistence. Instead, they serve as complementary measures that reflect how shape coexistence influences the fluctuation properties of low-lying spectra across different mass regions and spin sequences. The analysis incorporates both reported and unreported E2-active states to ensure that the statistical conclusions are based on complete experimental level sequences.

title: Polarized electron scattering from light nuclei at high energies
abstract: We present a theoretical approach to investigate the scattering of polarized electrons from light nuclei using the multipole expansion for the scattering cross section within the framework of the unified electroweak theory. The study is restricted to elastic and nuclear-level inelastic electron-nucleus scattering. Scattering processes corresponding to different electron polarizations are analyzed and compared with the unpolarized electron scattering investigated earlier. Besides, the contribution of both polarized and unpolarized terms to the scattering cross section is examined. Numerical calculations for stable 6,7 Li and unstable 7 Be nuclei using the Weinberg-Salam model show that the longitudinal polarization and weak interaction are not explicitly correlated when electrons scatter at θ ≃ 0 ∘ across all energy scales. A strong correlation emerges at the other scattering angles when the electron energy exceeds 10 GeV. This study provides additional information about nuclear structure and uncovers the role of electron polarization and its correlation with the weak interaction in each process, thus offering a more complete picture of electron-nucleus scattering.

title: Parity-pseudospin triplet bands in 153Eu
abstract: Excited states of 153 Eu have been investigated using in-beam γ -ray spectroscopy techniques with the 150 Nd( 7 Li, 4n) fusion-evaporation reaction at a beam energy of 42 MeV. Several new levels and transitions have been identified. Two positive-parity bands and one negative-parity band have been observed in 153 Eu, with the lifetimes of 5 high-spin states measured using the Doppler-shift-attenuation method (DSAM). The three rotational bands in 153 Eu exhibit similar experimental characteristics. Meanwhile, theoretical calculations based on the particle-rotor model with octupole deformation (PRM) indicate obvious mixing among the d 5/2 , g 7/2 , and h 11/2 configurations for the three bands. Therefore, the three nearly-degenerate bands in 153 Eu are interpreted as parity-pseudospin triplet bands. The present work reports the first parity-pseudospin triplet bands in nuclei, and provides evidence that pseudospin orbitals retain near degeneracy in an octupole-deformed potential.

title: Nuclear Structure of 118–132Xenon Nuclei: Insights from the IBM-2 Model
abstract: •Comprehensive systematic investigation of 118-132 Xe isotopes within the IBM-2 framework.•Detailed tracking the structural evolution from γsoft O(6) to vibrational U(5) symmetry approaching the N=82 shell closure•Identification of 128 Xe as a strong candidate for the E(5) critical point symmetry.•High-precision calculations of energy spectra, B(E2) and M1 transition rates, and mixing ratios.•Successful reproduction of the latest experimental data, confirming the predictive power of the model. This study focuses on investigating the nuclear structure of even-even xenon isotopes using the second interacting boson model (IBM-2). The study involves examining energy spectra and electromagnetic transitions in a wide range of xenon isotopes, in particular those with a nucleon number close to the magic number, N = 82. The IBM framework provides a simplified and insightful description of collective properties of atomic nuclei by treating nucleons as pairs of interacting bosons. By comparing experimental data with the computed calculations, we found valuable insights into the nuclear properties of 118–132 XE isotopes. A comparison with available experimental data shows overall a good agreement, particularly in the low-lying levels. The results show that light isotopes 118–126 Xe tend to possess γ-soft properties associated with O(6) symmetry, and the 128 Xe nucleus possesses E(5) properties. Heavy isotopes 130–132 Xe gradually tend to shift to U(5) symmetry as they approach shell closure at neutrons N = 82. The results not only improve understanding of xenon isotopes but also contribute to broader insights into atomic nuclei. Our work also provides a foundation to investigate the nuclear structure of other isotopes and to broaden our knowledge of the complex nature of the atomic nuclei.

title: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes
abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning–assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth–based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Gamow-Teller transitions and mirror energy differences for sd shell-nuclei using isospin non-conserving interaction
abstract: In the present work, isospin asymmetry in Gamow-Teller (GT) β-decay transitions for sd-shell mirror nuclei is investigated within the nuclear shell-model framework using the USDCm interaction. This interaction explicitly incorporates Coulomb and isospin non-conserving components, which enables a consistent description of mirror asymmetry parameters and mirror energy differences (MEDs). We have calculated the ft values, the mirror asymmetry parameter, and the MED values for a wide range of mirror nuclei with mass numbers A= 20, 21, 23, 24, 25, 26, 29 and 31, and the results are compared with the available experimental data. In many transitions, the isospin symmetry is weakly broken because the GT asymmetry parameters are very small. Also, significant deviations from the experimental values are observed for almost all the mirror nuclei. For several low-lying states, calculated MEDs show noticeable Thomas-Ehrman shift, underscoring the significant influence of Coulomb and isospin non-conserving effects in proton-rich systems. Overall, the general characteristics of GT strengths are reproduced by the USDCm interaction. The current study offers a comprehensive standard for comprehending isospin-symmetry breaking in sd-shell nuclei.

title: Coulomb and nuclear polarization of the nucleon density in the dinuclear configuration of the Ca 40 + Pb 208 system
abstract: The change of the nucleon density distribution of a heavy nucleus caused by the presence of a second nucleus at a fixed center-to-center distance is studied in the framework of the deformed Woods–Saxon mean field. The single-particle problem of one nucleus has been solved by diagonalization in a cylindrical harmonic-oscillator basis with the external field of the partner nucleus included in the Hamiltonian before diagonalization. The external field consists of the Coulomb potential of the partner charge distribution and of the nuclear part obtained by double folding of the Migdal density-dependent effective nucleon-nucleon interaction, in the same form as used in the dinuclear system approach. The induced density change δ ρ ( r ; R ) and the corresponding changes of the quadrupole moment, of the mean-square radius and of the interaction energy have been calculated for the Ca 40 + Pb 208 system at separations R = 15.5 – 20 fm. The results are compared with the first-order (linear-response) treatment of the same external field. Because the mean field is anchored at the origin, the multipole moments are shown to require a translationally invariant definition: a displaced but undeformed distribution acquires a quadrupole moment second order in the displacement, and in this problem that kinematic term is comparable with the induced moment itself. Once it is removed, the intrinsic quadrupole response of Pb 208 agrees with the first-order one to better than half a percent, and remains so over the full range of the switching parameter for the Coulomb field at R = 20 fm, while that of Ca 40 retains a genuine higher-order contribution of 12% to 16 % . The polarization of both partners is dominated by the repulsive Coulomb tidal field, which produces an oblate deformation of the density, while the attractive nuclear field acts in the opposite sense and partially cancels the Coulomb contribution at the smallest separations. At the larger separations the induced octupole deformation is close to 40 % of the quadrupole one for Pb 208 and to 50 % for Ca 40 , and it is the more sensitive indicator of the breakdown of the one-center picture. The polarization energy is a dipole quantity, the induced quadrupole deformation contributing only a few percent of it; it is verified by coupling-constant integration and is quoted under several correction prescriptions for the spurious translational component and for the absence of the residual interaction. The sensitivity to the geometry of the folding densities and the limits of validity of the one-center description are established quantitatively.

title: Glauber description of reaction cross sections with Bogoliubov many-body wave functions
abstract: I developed a microscopic framework that connects relativistic nuclear density functional theory to high-energy reaction observables by incorporating many-body Bogoliubov wavefunctions, represented in Pfaffian form, into the Monte Carlo integration of the Glauber model. This approach enables a simultaneous treatment of nuclear pairing correlations and multiple-scattering effects beyond the optical limit approximation (OLA). The method is applied to reaction cross sections of even-even O, Ne, and Mg isotopes on a $^{12}$C target. Complete multiple-scattering calculations systematically reduce the cross sections relative to the OLA and improves the agreement with measured interaction cross sections. Applications to the deformed Ne and Mg isotopes show that calculations based on a single intrinsic orientation depend strongly on the angle between the nuclear symmetry axis and the beam direction. Angular-momentum projection removes the spurious dependence on the arbitrarily selected intrinsic orientation and produces smooth isotopic systematics for the laboratory-frame cross sections. This work establishes a microscopic bridge between relativistic nuclear structure theory and reaction dynamics, providing a general framework for exploring exotic phenomena such as halos and clustering.

title: Nuclear binding, correlations, and the A dependence of the EMC effect
abstract: The measurements of inclusive electron scattering from nuclear targets carried out at the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility in the mid 2000s have provided valuable novel information on the A dependence of the modifications of nuclear structure functions known as the EMC effect. We argue that these data are best described in terms of the scaling variable y ̃ , designed to take into account dynamical effects in interacting many-particle systems, and analyze the A dependence of the slope of the inclusive cross-section ratios, R A = ( σ A / A ) / ( σ 2 / 2 ) , providing a measure of the size of the EMC effect in the region where nuclear binding plays a leading role. The results of our study clearly hint at a linear correlation between d R A ( y ̃ ) / d y ̃ and the average nucleon removal energy 〈 E A 〉 . The role of correlation effects in the determination of 〈 E A 〉 is highlighted.

title: Transverse-spin dependent energy-energy correlators in proton-proton collisions within the dihadron fragmentation framework
abstract: We calculate energy-energy correlations for two hadrons produced inside a jet in transversely polarized proton-proton collisions. We make numerical predictions based on a simple model that utilizes a previous global QCD analysis of dihadron fragmentation and transversity parton distribution functions. The results show remarkable agreement with a very recent STAR measurement. We also find the data at large jet transverse momentum have a slight preference for extractions of transversity that are consistent with lattice QCD computations of the nucleon tensor charges. Overall, this work provides further evidence for the underlying non-perturbative mechanism of near-side energy-energy correlators as well as highlights the potential for these observables to probe transverse-spin effects inside the nucleon.

title: Probing of incomplete fusion in closed shell nuclei
abstract: The excitation functions for eleven evaporation residues resulting from the interaction of 20 Ne-ion beam with 124 Sn target have been measured over an energy range of ≈ 127–165 MeV using the activation technique. The obtained excitation functions have been compared with theoretical predictions from the CASCADE code, which is based on the statistical model calculations. Both complete and incomplete fusion reaction channels have been identified through the analysis of experimental data, revealing the occurrence of incomplete fusion via the breakup of 20 Ne into 16 O + 4 He and 12 C + 8 Be, followed by the fusion of one of these fragments with the 124 Sn target nucleus. In these measurements, no significant pre-equilibrium particle emission has been found in the analysis with ALICE-91 code. On the other hand, the incomplete fusion fractions have been determined and analysed with different systems, considering parameters such as atomic number of target (ZT), mass number of target (AT), the fissionability parameter (Z 2 /A)T of the target, mass asymmetry, and target deformation. The lowest incomplete fusion fractions have been observed in the present system as compared to other systems at a constant normalizing parameter. Besides this, the analysis of ICF fractions with binding energy fraction (fB.E) shows an interesting valley of stability within the range 8.14 20 Ne-induced reactions when evaluated against the universal fusion function. Furthermore, the suppression factor has been analysed as a function of β2 to elucidate its systematic dependence of these parameters on CF. The present observations suggest that the suppression of ICF probability, even at energy higher than 30% above the Coulomb barrier, is associated with the shell closure effect of the magic nucleus target 124 Sn.

title: Measurement and compensation dynamic Lorentz force detuning of double-spoke cavity for CSNS-II
abstract: Dynamic Lorentz force detuning (LFD) in the 324 MHz superconducting double-spoke cavities for the China Spallation Neutron Source Phase-II (CSNS-II) linac is investigated through combined modeling, simulation, and cryomodule experiments. A modal ponderomotive coupling model is established and validated against multiphysics finite-element analysis and measurements up to 9 MV/m with 1.2 ms pulses at 50 Hz. Intra-pulse detuning reconstructed from low-level RF (LLRF) waveforms agrees with full-pulse detuning inferred from piezo-sensor signals, and FFT analysis identifies dominant mechanical modes consistent with simulated eigenfrequencies. Beyond single-cavity behavior, inter-cavity mechanical coupling through a shared cryomodule and support system is experimentally verified: RF excitation of one cavity induces measurable vibration and frequency perturbation in the adjacent cavity, confirmed independently by LLRF and piezo diagnostics. Active compensation is implemented with piezo tuners using a parameterized half-sine feedforward waveform. Parameters are first optimized by systematic scanning and then refined on-line using a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent interacting with the real cavity via a gymnasium/pyepics interface. After 1 0 4 training steps, the PPO-optimized waveform reduces the effective detuning metric by about 37% relative to the initial policy, matching or surpassing the best manually scanned setting while improving robustness to operating-condition variations.
